newsitem.title: USA: US Rep. Archer says Clinton tax cut short of goal.
newsitem.headline: US Rep. Archer says Clinton tax cut short of goal.

text.p: House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer said Wednesday that President Clinton's tax proposal fell far short of the $85 billion net tax cut called for in the five-year budget agreement.

The Texas Republican said an analysis of Clinton's tax plan showed it amounted to a $56.8 billion tax cut over five years. "This is a serious shortfall that, unless fixed, may complicate the prospects for passage of tax relief in the House," Archer said in a statement.

The shortfall resulted from the administration's ommission in its revenue tables of money raised from a proposed cigarette tax increase and the spending effect of increasing the earned income credit for the working poor, Archer said.
White House Budget Director Franklin Raines said Clinton's tax proposal did amount to an $85 billion net tax cut over five years.

"It is an $85 billion tax cut. The (earned income tax credit) is a tax cut for working people," Raines said. "Our view is the cigarette revenue ought to be set aside and put into a fund and only used for children and health issues," he said.
